         9                  ACTING PRESIDENT VALESKY:    The

        10       invocation today will be delivered by Rabbi

        11       Neal Joseph Loevinger, of Temple Beth El in

        12       Poughkeepsie, New York.

        13                  Rabbi.

        14                  RABBI LOEVINGER:    Thank you.

        15       Senator, Senator Saland, and all of those

        16       assembled, thank you for allowing me the honor

        17       of being here today.

        18                  In my tradition, the Jewish

        19       tradition, one of the names for God is "notein

        20       da'at," the giver of wisdom, or the source of

        21       wisdom.  So I will call upon that source of

        22       wisdom using these words in the hopes that we

        23       can all recognize a source of wisdom, whether

        24       we are of varying faiths or of no faith, a



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5004



         1       source of wisdom which allows human beings to

         2       transcend self-interest and come together and

         3       tend towards compassion and justice, mercy and

         4       inclusion.

         5                  So I ask the notein da'at, the

         6       source of our wisdom, to bless this Senate,

         7       its leaders and its advisors with the

         8       curiosity to seek new knowledge and the

         9       fearlessness to implement untried solutions to

        10       our state's challenges.

        11                  I ask our Source of Wisdom that

        12       this Senate should be blessed with the hearts

        13       of servants, servants who serve not great

        14       powers, but who serve the meekest of our

        15       citizens.  Bless this Senate to act as

        16       servants who can envision the needs of future

        17       generations and who are wise stewards of our

        18       state's natural and financial resources for

        19       future generations.

        20                  Please, Source of Wisdom, bless

        21       this Senate, its leaders and advisors with

        22       humility, so that all who come together here

        23       may set aside ego and immediate political

        24       consideration in order to forge compromises in



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5005



         1       the best interests of as many citizens as

         2       possible.

         3                  Please, Source of Wisdom, bless

         4       those who are gathered here today with

         5       openness of heart and openness of mind, to

         6       draw upon the insights of all the great faith

         7       traditions represented in our state, from

         8       those whose moral reasoning is grounded in

         9       traditions many thousands of years old, to

        10       those whose faith commitments cause them to

        11       seek new forms of social change.

        12                  Please, Source of Wisdom, bless all

        13       who are assembled here in the Senate with the

        14       grace of civility, to be examples for our

        15       citizenry of learning from our differences.

        16                  Please, Source of Wisdom, bless all

        17       who are assembled here today with the power of

        18       compassion to hear the cries of the

        19       broken-hearted and to respond with tenderness,

        20       insight, and a desire to heal.

        21                  Please, Source of Wisdom, bless all

        22       who are gathered here today with the

        23       remembrance that in a state as great as

        24       New York, our diversity is our strength and

        10                  SENATOR LIBOUS:    Explanation,

        13       Senator Hassell-Thompson, an explanation has

        15                  SENATOR HASSELL-THOMPSON:    Thank

        16       you, Mr. President.

        17                  Briefly, this bill gives the

        18       Legislature the authority to pass a law

        19       allowing inmates to work for not-for-profit

        20       agencies where appropriate and necessary.

        21                  ACTING PRESIDENT VALESKY:

        22       Senator Bonacic.

        23                  SENATOR BONACIC:    Thank you.

        24       Mr. President, I'd like to ask Senator



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5021



         1       Thompson a couple of questions, if I may.  If

         2       she will yield.

         3                  ACTING PRESIDENT VALESKY:

         4       Senator Hassell-Thompson, do you yield?

         5                  SENATOR HASSELL-THOMPSON:    Yes, I

         6       yield to the best of my ability.

         7                  ACTING PRESIDENT VALESKY:    The

         8       sponsor yields to the best of her ability.

         9                  SENATOR BONACIC:    Thank you,

        10       Senator Thompson.

        11                  Number one, this is a good bill.

        12       Whenever we can help our municipalities and

        13       our not-for-profit for volunteer work, that's

        14       something commendable.

        15                  The only thing I will ask you is

        16       this is going to be a constitutional change --

        17       I mean, a constitutional provision, and it's

        18       exclusively for those not-for-profits that are

        19       religious, charitable, or educational

        20       not-for-profits.

        21                  So I guess my first question is,

        22       should we define who they are?

        23                  SENATOR HASSELL-THOMPSON:    I'm

        24       not clear what -- through you, Mr. President.



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5022



         1       Senator Bonacic, I'm not sure -- I mean, I'm

         2       not clear what your question is.  Define in

         3       what manner?

         4                  SENATOR BONACIC:    Yes, Senator

         5       Thompson.  I'll give an example.  I form a

         6       not-for-profit to study the moon, and I get

         7       incorporated.  And I have a following, I'll

         8       call them moon followers, just for the

         9       purposes of our discussion.

        10                  It may not be, in our traditional

        11       sense, what a real not-for-profit is or is

        12       deserving.  And in our Constitution, it has

        13       never defined, nor has this Legislature

        14       defined, what is a legitimate religious

        15       not-for-profit, educational not-for-profit, or

        16       charitable not-for-profit.

        17                  And I'm making the suggestion, as

        18       this resolution goes forward, maybe we should

        19       define who they are.  That is my point to you.

        20       Is that something that you would give

        21       consideration to?

        22                  SENATOR HASSELL-THOMPSON:

        23       Through you, Mr. President.  The short answer

        24       to your question, Senator Bonacic, is

         1       absolutely.

         2                  The long answer to your question is

         3       I guess my concern is that while I think it's

         4       important that we all be very clear about who

         5       we're talking about, when in fact an

         6       organization is given the status of

         7       not-for-profit, isn't it then up to the

         8       authorizing agency, usually the State

         9       Department, to make that determination as to

        10       whether or not, through its examination and

        11       through its criteria, they have therefore

        12       determined that this is in fact a

        13       not-for-profit?

        14                  Therefore, how do we define, as you

        15       put it, legitimacy?  Do you understand what

        16       I'm saying?

        17                  SENATOR BONACIC:    I do.  I do.

        18                  SENATOR HASSELL-THOMPSON:    And so

        19       that's why I asked you to define the question.

        20       Because if in fact they are given the title

        21       not-for-profit, and if they actually have the

        22       501(c)(3), 501(c)(6), 10, whatever the

        23       category is, they are legitimate as the law

        24       prescribes.

                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         5024



         1                  If you feel that there is another

         2       way in which we need to do that defining, then

         3       I'll go back to my short answer:  Absolutely.

         4                  SENATOR BONACIC:    Okay.  If

         5       Senator Thompson will continue to yield.

         6                  ACTING PRESIDENT VALESKY:

         7       Senator Hassell-Thompson, do you continue to

         8       yield?

         9                  SENATOR HASSELL-THOMPSON:    Yes.

        10                  ACTING PRESIDENT VALESKY:    The

        11       sponsor continues.

        12                  SENATOR BONACIC:    It's my

        13       understanding that those officials that

        14       receive a not-for-profit application, it is

        15       more a legal act of making sure your T's are

        16       crossed and your I's are dotted, and no

        17       judgment as to whether the purpose of the

        18       not-for-profit is legitimate or not within our

        19       traditional concepts.

        20                  And the reason I am having this

        21       discussion with you is, to refresh your

        22       recollection, we develop legislation for

        23       tax-exempts and the abuses for

        24       not-for-profits.  And we got into this issue.

         1                  And over the last 30 years, the

         2       courts have defined what a legitimate

         3       not-for-profit could be.  And I will give you

         4       one example.  One man, saying "I believe in

         5       God" -- no church, no followers -- got

         6       tax-exempt status on hundreds of acres that he

         7       bought.

         8                  And that was, in my opinion, an

         9       abuse of what should be tax-exempt.  Because
